column2: Table 9: Quantitative Comparison of Paper 2 (Gandhi et al. 2024) and Proposed Framework on Java Source-Code Plagiarism Detection

Side-by-side comparison on the same held-out Java test partition (N=210 pairs, IR-Plag cases 06-07). Paper 2 = repository-audited reproduction of Gandhi et al. (2024) adapted to Java (7-D syntactic/token features + RBF-SVM, threshold 0.3700). Proposed = Condition C typed-decision tri-band pipeline with SVM heavy verifier. Differences follow the signed improvement convention.
IR-Plag Java Corpus, Policy A (720 pairs across 7 programming assignments; zero program sharing across cases, SHA-256 verified)
Case-disjoint holdout: cases 01-04 training (416 pairs), case-05 validation (107 pairs), cases 06-07 test (210 pairs; 102 plagiarized / 108 non-plagiarized)

SVC(kernel='rbf', C=1.0, gamma='scale', probability=True, random_state=42) over 7-D features (raw/anonymized token Jaccard, keyword-distribution cosine, operator Jaccard, line-count ratio, cyclomatic-complexity differential, character 3-grams); StandardScaler; decision threshold 0.3700 (F1-tuned on case-05); exhaustive scoring of all pairs

Token-Jaccard cheap pre-filter; tri-band routing theta_low=0.61 / theta_high=0.87 (case-05 tuned, target candidate recall >= 0.98); SVM heavy verifier (same configuration as Paper 2) invoked only on uncertain band; direct high-risk flags bypass the verifier

Both sides: reproduced implementation results, exactly matching the archived verified record (experiments/results/code_results_detailed.json; final_comparison_table.csv). ROC-AUC/PR-AUC for the proposed condition: N/A (discrete band decisions). Memory: N/R (not instrumented). Latency rows use non-comparable accounting (see notes): paper = classifier-only inference; proposed = end-to-end tri-band pipeline.
